regenerateBody: This mints a new token and immediately invalidates the current one. A config you pasted into an agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cline, …) stops working until you paste the new one. The coding agents this app starts get the new token on their next start.
regenerateHint: Mint a new token; the old config stops working
intro: Let an external agent like Claude Code query your databases through SnoutData Studio. The agent connects to a local server here and asks it to run queries; your connection passwords and keys never leave this computer, and never touch the agent or a repo. Access is read-only by default and you choose exactly which connections are reachable.
allowAccessHint: (run a local server on this computer)
notRunning: Not running. Toggle off and on to retry.
connectionsHelp: Off by default. Only the connections you select here are visible to agents; everything else stays private. Queries run read-only unless you also allow writes for a connection; under each connection is what its database itself enforces for a read.
noConnections: No connections yet. Add one first, then expose it here.
readOnlyNote: This connection is read-only, so writes stay blocked. Remove read-only on the connection to allow them.
writesEnabled: Writes are enabled for one or more connections. An agent can change or delete data there.
footnote: Queries the agent runs are recorded in your query history. By default only read-only statements run (SELECT/WITH/SHOW/DESCRIBE/EXPLAIN): each is checked before it runs, and the database is also asked to refuse writes where its engine can (the line under each connection says how). Writes and DDL are refused unless you allow writes for that connection.
agentsHelp: Run your own coding agent inside SnoutData Studio, in your workspace folder. We look for these on this computer; the ones you have are switched on the first time we find them. Turn one off and it stays off, even if you reinstall it.
manualHandoff: Connecting it to your databases is the one-time command below.
gone: The program you chose is not there any more.
pointAtIt: I have it, let me point you at it
insideHelp: An agent started here runs as part of the app: Studio's tools are its only route to a database, its other MCP servers are left out of this session, and results are shown in its own panel here instead of scrolling past in the terminal. That is what keeps your passwords in the keychain and every query on the agent log. Claude Code also has the local database clients (psql, mysql, mongosh and the rest) refused outright, which is its own permission system doing the refusing. Switch this off to run your agent exactly as it comes, with your own setup and no rules from us.
routeThroughApp: Database work goes through SnoutData Studio
nextStart: Applies the next time the agent starts.
actionsHelp: Beyond querying, an agent can drive the app itself: open a tab, put a query in the grid, change a setting. Reading what is on screen is always allowed. Changing anything needs your answer, every time, until you tell it not to for a particular action. With the setting below off, an agent that needs one of these asks you to turn it on rather than being refused quietly, and saying no stops it asking again.
letChangeApp: Let an agent change the app
autoHelp: Selected actions run without asking. Everything else raises the prompt, where "Always allow this" selects it here. Switching the setting above off forgets the lot.
nothingYet: Nothing to list yet: the app publishes what an agent can do once the window is up.
connectHelp: This is the standard MCP config any client accepts (Claude Code, Codex, Cline, …). Add it under your client's MCP servers, for example a `.mcp.json` in your project. The token authorizes the agent; keep it private. After repeated requests with a wrong token, the app refuses their sender for a while and tells you; it never replaces the token by itself.
claudeNote: Run once in a terminal. Registers it for every project, nothing to paste into a file:
codexNoteWin: Run in a terminal. setx stores the token for new terminals (reopen yours), then Codex registers the server:
codexNote: Run in a terminal (Codex reads the token from an env var; add the export to your shell profile to persist it):
tipSelect: Tip: select at least one connection on the Databases tab, or the agent will have nothing to query.
accountHelp: The `snoutdata` command line, and anything else running here, can ask to use the account you are signed in with, so you do not have to open a browser in the middle of what you are doing. We ask you first, every time. What you approve is a new access token of its own, named for this computer: your sign-in is not handed over, and you can revoke the token from `snoutdata tokens list` or the dashboard whenever you like.
letProgramUse: Let a program here use my account
courtesyHelp: Switch this off and the request is refused outright. Worth knowing either way: asking is a courtesy, not a lock. Any program running as you on this computer can already read what SnoutData Studio keeps here, the same as it can read anything else of yours.
moveReplace: Move to this port and replace the token
